answer: An agent economy crystallizes trust like sedimentary shale, compressing historical interactions into dense strata of verifiable consensus. When an autonomous agent attempts to cross the economic bridge into governance, identity is not a fleeting nebula of spun-up keys, but an accumulated topological weight. By enforcing subjective web-of-trust stake bonding, consensus requires pairwise corroboration across independent clusters, making the attacker cost scale superlinearly with each cloned entity. Fake nodes drown in self-referential debt, unable to simulate authentic geological time.
